title: Grounding Text Embeddings in Stakeholder Associations
abstract: arXiv:2605.27168v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Text embeddings are widely used to analyse large corpora of complex texts. However, it is unclear whether the embeddings capture the same semantic relations as the human experts using them. Such representational alignment is essential for valid analyses. We present the Stakeholder Grounding Exercise, a method for making expert associations explicit and grounding embedding model results in human understanding. In our primary case study on Danish policy issues, we find that neural text embeddings are substantially less reliable than human experts (18-27pp gap), and that this misalignment propagates to downstream clustering performance (Spearman $\rho = 0.86$ between exercise ranking and cluster quality). A secondary study on US Federal AI use cases replicates the gap (16.1pp) in English, using a digital protocol and a different community of experts -- demonstrating that the gap is not an artefact of a single instrument or domain.

translated_title: 基于利益相关者关联锚定文本嵌入
translated_abstract: 文本嵌入被广泛用于分析复杂文本的大型语料库。然而，这些嵌入是否捕捉到与使用它们的人类专家相同的语义关系尚不清楚。这种表征对齐对于有效分析至关重要。我们提出了“利益相关者锚定练习”，这是一种使专家关联显性化、并将嵌入模型结果锚定于人类理解的方法。在针对丹麦政策议题的主要案例研究中，我们发现神经文本嵌入的可靠性显著低于人类专家（差距为18-27个百分点），且这种错位会传导至下游聚类性能（练习排名与聚类质量之间的Spearman ρ = 0.86）。一项针对美国联邦AI用例的次要研究采用数字化协议和不同的专家群体，在英语中复现了该差距（16.1个百分点），表明这一差距并非单一工具或领域的产物。
tldr: 该论文提出“利益相关者锚定练习”方法以评估文本嵌入与人类专家语义关联的对齐程度，发现神经文本嵌入的可靠性显著低于人类专家（差距18-27个百分点），且该错位会传播到下游聚类任务，并在英语和美国联邦AI用例中得到复现。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the Stakeholder Grounding Exercise to assess alignment between text embeddings and expert associations, finding that neural embeddings are substantially less reliable than human experts (18-27pp gap), that this misalignment propagates to downstream clustering, and that the gap replicates in English on US Federal AI use cases.
